IMPORTANT: Admission is subject to performance in the written exam.
Students with an addiction history will not be admitted.
An undertaking / indemnity on a ₹500 bond is mandatory.
Over-age students will not be enrolled.
Strict disciplinary action is taken against those who break the rules.
FEES: Fees are collected in two terms.
The first instalment is paid once admission is confirmed.
The second instalment is paid in the second semester, after the Diwali holiday.
For the balance, parents submit a post-dated cheque along with a promissory note.
Competitive coaching courses attract extra fees.

FAQ.question: Which levels does the Panchgani campus offer?
FAQ.answer: Primary, High School (SSC) and Jr. College (HSC), all English-medium.

FAQ.question: Is coaching for NEET, JEE, CET, NATA and CA included?
FAQ.answer: Coaching is offered on campus. Competitive courses attract extra fees.

FAQ.question: What is the admission process?
FAQ.answer: Parents’ interview, child’s interview, written exam, medical history and — from Std 8 — a blood investigation.

FAQ.question: How are fees paid?
FAQ.answer: In two terms: after admission is confirmed and after the Diwali holiday. A post-dated cheque and promissory note secure the balance.

FAQ.question: What medical care is available?
FAQ.answer: A trained nurse is on campus 24/7, a doctor visits for check-ups and the sick bay can keep patients in-house.

FAQ.question: Is prayer compulsory?
FAQ.answer: The call to prayer is given five times a day and Muslim students are expected to offer salah. Basic Islamic education and Quran recitation are emphasised.

FAQ.question: Are there supports for students who struggle?
FAQ.answer: Yes — peer tutors, resident advisors, academic advisors and extra coaching for vernacular-medium students.

FAQ.question: How will my child be looked after day to day?
FAQ.answer: A dorm in-charge looks after each dormitory, academic advisors meet students regularly to set goals, and a trained nurse is on campus 24/7.

FAQ.question: Will my child get individual attention?
FAQ.answer: Peer tutors and resident advisors support evening study, advisors track each student’s progress, and extra coaching is provided for vernacular-medium students who need it.

FAQ.question: What will my child eat?
FAQ.answer: Five meals a day in a renovated dining hall for 300, on a menu designed by a dietician. The kitchen is supervised throughout.

FAQ.question: What does my child do besides studying?
FAQ.answer: Sports, archery, horse riding, skating, robotics, drama, debate, pottery, gardening and more, with inter-house competitions through the year.

FAQ.question: Which examinations do students sit?
FAQ.answer: The school prepares students for the Maharashtra SSC (Std X) and HSC (Std XII) examinations.
